tool_input.command: cd <repo> && git status --porcelain -- crates/lights && echo '=== log for descent.rs ===' && git log --oneline -5 -- crates/lights/src/fit/descent.rs && echo '=== tests referencing descent ===' && grep -rln 'descent' crates/lights/tests/
tool_input.description: Check git state of descent.rs
Run descent tests, capture the sweep table

tool_input.content:
import json

RECORD = "docs/lights/RESEARCH.json"

rec = {
    "slug": "l131-finite-difference-gradient",
    "title": "Can a central-difference gradient of the fit loss be trusted at this crate's curvature, and which step size does the sweep choose?",
    "group": "engineering",
    "date": "2026-09-15",
    "verdict": "Yes, at eps = 1e-6, and the plateau was MEASURED rather than assumed: |g| agrees to seven digits across 1e-5/1e-6/1e-7 and the directional-derivative identity holds to 8.2e-10 of |g| there. The module's first choice, 1e-4, was REFUSED by its own sweep. The failure modes are not the textbook two: besides curvature at large eps and cancellation below 1e-8, there is a third that is NOT monotone in eps — a support-edge straddle, which made 1e-4 (identity error 8.3e-3) worse than both its neighbours (3.6e-5 at 1e-3, 9.2e-9 at 1e-5) through the angle partial alone. The vector is also usable: from the point where the coordinate ladder is stuck on t5-thin-stroke it still descends, by 1.004e-2 relative in 20 steps — so the mechanism L-131 named is real in sign, and small on this target.",
    "question": "BURNDOWN L-131. The crate's only search is a coordinate ladder (greedy::refine) that accepts a step only when ONE knob lowers the energy on its own, and P2_RESULTS.md:67 reports 'in 20 of 24 cells the fitter stopped, not the budget'. Before any optimiser is written: can the nine per-parameter partials of the loss be assembled into one vector by finite differences and trusted? Too large a step measures curvature, too small measures floating-point cancellation, and both produce a plausible-looking vector pointing somewhere else — so which step, chosen from a measured table rather than a guess, and is the resulting direction one the ladder's stuck point actually has?",
    "command": "cargo test -p lights --all-features --test fit_descent -- --test-threads 1 --nocapture\n\nRun 2026-09-15 on the M5 Max: 6 passed, 0 failed, finished in 1.05 s. Every figure below is printed by that one invocation and is deterministic (render counts and residual energies, not timings). The sweep table comes from the_step_sweep_measures_a_flat_middle_and_the_chosen_step_names_its_row; the stuck-ladder figures from the_ladder_stops_where_the_descent_direction_still_lowers_the_energy; the identity errors from the_directional_derivative_identity_holds_at_the_chosen_step.",
    "criterion": "Written into L-131 before the module existed, as two checks that can fail plus one discriminating case. (a) THE IDENTITY: for a unit direction d with every component non-zero, (loss(x + eps d) - loss(x - eps d)) / (2 eps) must agree with g . d to a stated tolerance — 1e-3 of |g| here — which catches a wrong sign, a wrong scaling and a missing partial at once. (b) THE STEP SWEEP: the gradient is taken at ten decades, 1e-1 to 1e-10, on one real atom, and the chosen step must be a row of that table whose change from its neighbour is below 1e-6 relative while BOTH ends of the sweep change more, so the flat middle is measured and not assumed. (c) THE DISCRIMINATING CASE: converge the ladder on Target::t5_thin_stroke until an extra sweep returns the energy bit-identical, then require that a line search along the projected gradient still lowers it, and that 20 steps of steepest descent gain more than 1e-3 relative. Target, viewport 64x64 from t5_thin_stroke, gaussian kernel, SharedSettings::prefiltered, tile 16, truth from exact_coverage at quadrature depth 10.",
    "numbers": [
        {
            "label": "the flat middle: gradient norm across the sweep",
            "value": "4.025793e1 at 1e-5, 1e-6 and 1e-7 — identical to seven digits; 3.232351e0 at 1e-1 and 4.025794e1 at 1e-10",
            "note": "Sweep table, column |g|, on the one-atom fit of t5-thin-stroke. The 1e-1 row is a factor of 12 low because at that step the angle probe swings the 15 px atom right off its own support: its angle partial is -2.046 against the plateau's -40.18."
        },
        {
            "label": "the chosen step names its row",
            "value": "eps = 1e-6, change from the decade above 3.394e-8 — the smallest in the table; 1e-2 changes by 9.453e-1, 1e-10 by 7.121e-6",
            "note": "Sweep table, column change_vs_prev. CHOSEN_STEP in src/fit/descent.rs is 1e-6 and tests/fit_descent.rs asserts that row is flatter than both ends, so the constant cannot drift away from the measurement silently."
        },
        {
            "label": "identity error at the chosen step",
            "value": "8.175e-10 of |g| on the fitted atom (|g| = 4.025793e1); 2.301e-10 on an independent interior atom (|g| = 4.917810e1); tolerance 1e-3",
            "note": "the_directional_derivative_identity_holds_at_the_chosen_step. The same test first asserts every one of the nine partials is non-zero on the interior atom, so a gradient that skipped a parameter could not pass by cancellation."
        },
        {
            "label": "THE THIRD FAILURE MODE: a support-edge straddle at 1e-4, non-monotone in eps",
            "value": "identity error 8.297e-3 at 1e-4, against 3.642e-5 at 1e-3 and 9.224e-9 at 1e-5 — worse than BOTH neighbours",
            "note": "Sweep table. The per-parameter rows localise it to one partial: angle is -4.04017e1 at 1e-4 against -4.01766e1 on the plateau, while the other eight equal the plateau to six digits. The fitted atom is 15 px long and a third of a pixel thin (log-scales 2.728975 and -1.117325), so 1e-4 rad tilts its tips by 4.5e-3 px and one probe crossed a pixel centre through the splat's hard alpha-cutoff support edge."
        },
        {
            "label": "the cancellation side",
            "value": "change_vs_prev 1.164e-7 at 1e-8, 6.856e-7 at 1e-9, 7.121e-6 at 1e-10",
            "note": "Sweep table. The per-parameter rows show it arriving in the smallest partials first: the three colour partials sit at -9.16955e-3 through the plateau and split to -9.04166e-3 / -9.07718e-3 at 1e-10, while centre.x still holds five digits."
        },
        {
            "label": "cost of one gradient",
            "value": "18 renders, exactly 2 per parameter; the ten-decade sweep costs 200",
            "note": "a_gradient_costs_eighteen_renders_and_bills_its_own_site asserts budget.used() rises by RENDERS_PER_GRADIENT = 2 * P and that the site string is fit::descent::gradient, so gradient renders are never attributed to fit::greedy::fit."
        },
        {
            "label": "the ladder's stuck point, and that the gradient is not zero there",
            "value": "energy 23.072884 after 5 extra full sweeps that changed nothing; |g| = 3.908354e1, of which the angle partial is -3.900833e1",
            "note": "the_ladder_stops_where_the_descent_direction_still_lowers_the_energy. Stuck is asserted, not assumed: one more refine() call must return the energy bit-identical before the gradient is taken. No component of the projected direction is clipped by the box, so this is not a constrained stationary point."
        },
        {
            "label": "how far the descent direction walks out of the ladder's stop",
            "value": "one line-searched step of length 2^-9 = 1.953125e-3 reaches 23.024982 (2.076e-3 relative); 20 steps of steepest descent reach 22.841347 (1.004e-2 relative) for 721 renders",
            "note": "Same test, floor 1e-3 relative. The atom moves 0.1298 px in centre.x and 5.157e-3 rad in angle — both far below the ladder's smallest centre step of 8 * 2^-7 = 0.0625, which is why no single knob could see the improvement."
        }
    ],
    "findings": [
        "THE STEP SIZE IS NOT A FREE PARAMETER AND THE SWEEP CAUGHT A WRONG ONE. src/fit/descent.rs first shipped CHOSEN_STEP = 1e-4, chosen before the sweep was run; the sweep's identity column refused it at 8.3e-3 and the table moved the constant to 1e-6. This is the instrument catching its own author, which is the whole reason L-131 demanded the sweep before the optimiser.",
        "THERE IS A THIRD FAILURE MODE AND IT IS NOT MONOTONE IN EPS. The textbook picture is curvature above and cancellation below with a valley between, so a bisection on eps would find a good step. On this loss it would not: 1e-4 is a spike between two agreeing rows. The cause is that the splat's alpha cutoff gives every pixel a hard support edge, so the loss is piecewise-smooth, and a central difference is essentially exact BETWEEN crossings and wrong ACROSS one. The good step is the one that rarely straddles, not one that never does.",
        "THE IDENTITY CHECK IS THE STRADDLE DETECTOR, which is why it is run at every row of the sweep rather than once at the chosen step. A straddled axis probe moves g . d without moving the directional probe, so the two estimates separate; the gradient norm alone would not have flagged 1e-4 (4.048259e1 against 4.025793e1, half a percent).",
        "THE MECHANISM L-131 NAMED IS REAL. The ladder converges to a point where the gradient is 39 in norm and unclipped by the box, and a line search along it immediately lowers the energy. A coordinate ladder and a gradient are demonstrably not the same search on this loss.",
        "AND IT IS SHALLOW ON THIS TARGET. 1.004e-2 relative for 721 renders. The entry's sentence that the ladder stops 'at a point a descent direction would walk straight out of' is true in sign and about one percent in size on t5-thin-stroke, so L-132's case must be made on the classes P2 reported stopping early, not on this one.",
        "THE PARAMETER VECTOR IS RAW. pack/unpack carry no clamp and no angle wrap; the box enters only through projected_descent and clamp_to. A difference quotient is therefore always taken about the point that was asked for, and a boundary is handled by projecting the direction rather than by silently shortening the probe — which would have made the partial a lie about the loss."
    ],
    "refuted": [
        "CHOSEN_STEP = 1e-4, the module's own first choice, refused by its own step sweep at an identity error of 8.297e-3 against a 1e-3 tolerance.",
        "The two-sided picture of finite-difference error implied by L-131's own next field — 'too large a step measures curvature instead of slope, too small a step measures floating-point cancellation' — as a COMPLETE account. It is complete for a smooth loss; this loss has hard support edges and the error is not monotone on either side of the plateau.",
        "That the gradient norm is a sufficient diagnostic for step choice. It is flat to half a percent across the bad row."
    ],
    "not_settled": [
        "Whether eps = 1e-6 transfers. The plateau was measured on ONE atom (the one-atom fit of t5-thin-stroke) at ONE viewport (64x64) with ONE kernel (gaussian). The straddle argument says the plateau's width scales with the support perimeter, so a much larger atom or a much larger viewport may move it; nothing here measures that.",
        "The straddle explanation itself is a mechanism, not a measurement: no test isolates a pixel crossing. It is consistent with every column of the table and with the atom's geometry, and it is written down so it can be refuted.",
        "Multi-atom gradients. gradient() takes an index and perturbs one atom; the cross terms between atoms are never formed. Joint optimisation and the prefix contract are L-132's.",
        "Whether descent beats the ladder on cost. 18 renders per gradient against the ladder's 2 per knob per halving is a comparison nobody has tabulated, and 721 renders for 1e-2 relative is not obviously a good trade.",
        "Whether the gain is material on the classes P2 reported stopping early. That is exactly L-132's close bar and then L-43's measurement.",
        "descend() is steepest descent with a halving line search, built to measure the gap, not the optimiser L-132 owes: no momentum, no Adam, no seeding, no prefix contract, one atom."
    ],
    "artefacts": [
        "crates/lights/src/fit/descent.rs (the instrument)",
        "crates/lights/src/fit/descent_rs_comment/finite_difference_instrument.md (the prose, including the straddle account)",
        "crates/lights/tests/fit_descent.rs (6 tests; prints every table above under --nocapture)",
        "docs/lights/mutations/results.tsv rows 345-351, seven mutations on src/fit/descent.rs, all CAUGHT through all four gates"
    ],
    "sources": [
        "crates/lights/src/fit/greedy.rs (refine, the coordinate ladder; evaluate, the loss; KNOBS and LADDER_LEVELS)",
        "crates/lights/src/fit/atom2d.rs (Atom2d and the parameter order pack/unpack follows)",
        "crates/lights/src/blend.rs (the alpha cutoff that gives each pixel a hard support edge)",
        "crates/lights/head_open.toml L-131, L-132 and L-43",
        "docs/lights/P2_RESULTS.md:67 ('in 20 of 24 cells the fitter stopped, not the budget')",
        "docs/plan/TWO_HORIZON_PLAN.md:482-501 (the gradient-fitter prerequisite as originally written)"
    ],
}

doc = json.load(open(RECORD))
doc["records"] = [r for r in doc["records"] if r["slug"] != rec["slug"]] + [rec]
with open(RECORD, "w") as fh:
    json.dump(doc, fh, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    fh.write("\n")
print("records now", len(doc["records"]))
